## Learning objectives

By the end of this activity, you should be able to inspect the project's R
lockfile, explain how a Docker image becomes a Binder session, and record the
environment used to load the teaching data.

Complete [preparation](00_preparation.qmd) before the session, including the
data download and environment checks. Run the R activities in a prepared
MyBinder session or an existing local R environment.

## Why this matters

The same script can behave differently when package versions or system
libraries change. We need to describe the environment alongside the code and
the data version.

| Layer | What we record | Tool or file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R runtime | R version | `renv.lock`, runtime information, container base image |
| R packages | Package versions and sources | renv and `renv.lock` |
| Wider environment | Operating-system libraries and rendering tools | Dockerfile and image |
| Code and configuration | The revision used for the run | Git commit |
| Actual session | Versions loaded when the activity ran | `sessionInfo()` |

renv restores the R packages described by a lockfile. A Docker image can also
include the R interpreter, operating-system libraries, and rendering tools.
Reproducing a result still requires the analysis code, the input data, and a
successful rerun.

## Inspect the current environment

Allow about two minutes. In the **R Console**, with the project open:

```{r health-environments-session, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
R.version.string
.libPaths()
packageVersion("renv")
```

Compare your R version with the reference version, **4.4.1**. If it differs,
record the difference; a lockfile does not switch your running R session.

## Inspect and restore a lockfile

Allow about four minutes. Use the project's active renv environment:

```{r health-environments-lockfile, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
lock <- renv::lockfile_read("renv.lock")
lock$R$Version
names(lock$Packages)
renv::status()
```

The lockfile names R 4.4.1 and records package versions for the workshop,
including `meta`, `codebook`, `dataspice`, `pins`, and `targets`.
Use `renv::status()` to check whether your active library matches the lockfile.

The usual collaboration cycle is:

1. A maintainer prepares and tests the required packages.
2. The maintainer uses `renv::snapshot()` and reviews the resulting lockfile.
3. Collaborators use `renv::restore()` to obtain the recorded packages.
4. The analysis is tested in the restored environment.

For this activity, inspect the existing lockfile. The Binder image is built
with the restored library. If you are setting up local R, follow the
[preparation instructions](00_preparation.qmd) to restore it before the workshop.

## From a Dockerfile to RStudio on MyBinder {#environments-docker}

Allow about four minutes. Participants need a browser to use MyBinder. The
build commands below show what runs on GitHub Actions, so you can follow along
without installing Docker or running a build.

### Read the Dockerfile

A **Dockerfile** is a set of instructions for building a Docker image. Find
these instructions in the workshop's [Binder image Dockerfile](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/blob/main/dockerfiles/binder/Dockerfile.1.0.0).

| Instruction | What it does in this project |
| --- | --- |
| `FROM rocker/binder:4.4.1 AS base` | Starts from Rocker’s Binder image for R 4.4.1. |
| `RUN` | Executes build steps such as installing system libraries and restoring R packages from `renv.lock`. |
| `COPY` | Adds files such as the lockfile and workshop lessons to the image. |

A **Docker build** uses these instructions and the repository files to produce
an **image**. A **container** is a running instance of an image. The image
provides the environment, and each participant runs the workshop in their own
container.

### Follow the GitHub Actions build pipelines

The repository has two workflows that run when a GitHub release is published
or when a maintainer starts them manually. [Build Binder](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/actions/workflows/build-binder.yaml)
builds the image MyBinder uses. [Build RStudio](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/actions/workflows/build-rstudio.yaml)
builds a separate image for people running RStudio with Docker locally.

Each workflow checks out the source, reads `VERSION` into `APP_VERSION`, and
records a UTC build date. Docker Compose uses `APP_VERSION` to select the
Dockerfile and tag the image. The binder job includes these two steps.

```bash
docker compose build binder
docker compose push binder
```

The first command builds the image. The second publishes the image with its
version tag to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`). The image version comes
from `VERSION` and can differ from the GitHub release tag. Open a completed
workflow run and find its build and push output if you want to see the process
in the Actions log.

### Launch the published environment

MyBinder reads the small [Binder entry point](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/blob/main/binder/Dockerfile),
which selects the published Binder image with `FROM`. MyBinder prepares the
launch image and starts a container on its servers. The launch link’s
`urlpath=rstudio` setting opens the RStudio interface in your browser.

Use the session you opened during [preparation](00_preparation.qmd#choose-your-computing-environment)
to run the R exercises. Keep your project files and outputs together in that
session, and download your work before it ends.

## Try it yourself: restart, reload, record

Allow about three minutes. Restart R, reopen the project if necessary, and load
the data from its explicit path. This checks that the input does not depend on
an object left over from an earlier Console session.

```{r health-environments-reload, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
stopifnot(
  file.exists(raw_file),
  identical(
    unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file)),
    "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"
  )
)
data_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = data_env)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
health <- data_env[["HealthWellbeing"]]
stopifnot(nrow(health) == 29L, ncol(health) == 5L)

output_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(
  capture.output(sessionInfo()),
  file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt")
)
```

Inspect `outputs/session-info.txt`. Add a short sentence to your existing
`WORKSHOP_NOTES.md` recording the R version and whether you used MyBinder or
local R. If you used MyBinder, record the image tag from `binder/Dockerfile`
and the project revision from `git rev-parse HEAD` in the **Terminal**. Keep
the raw data and generated session record separate from code changes.

## Checkpoint {#environments-checkpoint}

- You can explain which parts of the environment renv and Docker capture.
- You can trace how GitHub Actions builds and publishes the Binder image and
  how MyBinder uses it to start RStudio.
- You can distinguish the lockfile's requested R version from the running version.
- The dataset reloads after a restart, and you have a session record on disk.
- You can identify the workshop package versions recorded in the lockfile.

**Takeaway:** a documented environment supports reproducibility, and a successful
rerun supplies evidence. Next, the programme turns to dataset documentation and
FAIR metadata with codebook and dataspice.
[Dataset documentation](04_data_documentation.qmd)
